text:
THE DUENNA (in rapture):
  Oh, look! The knocker is wrapped in cloths!...
  (To the knocker):
  They have gagged you so that your metal
  Will not disturb the lovely speeches—little brute!
  (She lifts it with infinite care and knocks softly.)

ROXANE (seeing that the door is being opened):
  Let us go in!...
  (From the threshold, to Cyrano):
  If Christian comes, as I presume he will,
  Let him wait for me!

CYRANO (quickly, as she is about to disappear):
  Ah!...
  (She turns around):
  On what, as is your custom,
  Do you intend to question him today?

ROXANE:
  On...

CYRANO (quickly):
  On?

ROXANE:
  But you will keep silent about it!

CYRANO:
  Like a wall.

ROXANE:
  On nothing!... I shall tell him: Go on! Set forth with no rein!
  Improvise. Speak of love. Be splendid!

CYRANO (smiling):
  Good.

ROXANE:
  Hush!...

CYRANO:
  Hush!...

ROXANE:
  Not a word!...
  (She goes inside and closes the door again.)

CYRANO (bowing to her once the door is closed):
  With thanks to you.
  (The door opens again and Roxane puts her head out.)

ROXANE:
  He might prepare himself!...

CYRANO:
  Good heavens, no!...

BOTH TOGETHER:
  Hush!...
  (The door closes.)

CYRANO (calling):
  Christian!



Scene 3.IV.

Cyrano, Christian.


CYRANO:
  I know everything we need. Ready thy memory.
  Here is the chance to cover oneself with glory.
  Let us waste no time. Do not look so sullen.
  Quickly, let us go back to thy lodgings; I am going to teach thee...

CHRISTIAN:
  No!

CYRANO:
  What?

CHRISTIAN:
  No! I am waiting for Roxane here.

CYRANO:
  What fit of madness
  Has seized thee? Come quickly and learn...

CHRISTIAN:
  No, I tell thee!
  I am weary of borrowing my letters, my speeches,
  And of playing this part, and of always trembling!...
  It was all very well at first! But I feel that she loves me!
  Thank you. I am no longer afraid. I shall speak for myself.

CYRANO:
  Indeed!

CHRISTIAN:
  And who tells thee that I would not know how?...
  I am not so stupid, after all! Thou shalt see!
  But, my dear fellow, thy lessons have been useful to me.
  I shall know how to speak alone! And, by all the devils,
  I shall certainly always know how to take her in my arms!...
  (Catching sight of Roxane, who is coming out of Clomire’s house again):
  —It is she! Cyrano, no, do not leave me!

CYRANO (bowing to him):
  Speak by yourself, sir.
  (He disappears behind the garden wall.)



Scene 3.V.

Christian, Roxane, several précieuses and their admirers, and the duenna,
for a moment.


ROXANE (leaving Clomire’s house with a company from which she now
  parts, amid curtsies and bows):
  Barthénoïde!—Alcandre!—Grémione!...

THE DUENNA (in despair):
  We missed the discourse on the Tender!
  (She goes into Roxane’s house.)

ROXANE (still taking her leave):
  Urimédonte!... Farewell!...
  (They all bow to Roxane, bow to one another again, part, and
  go off down different streets. Roxane sees Christian):
  It is you!...
  (She goes to him):
  Evening is falling.
  Wait. They are far away. The air is mild. Not a passerby.
  Let us sit down. Speak. I am listening.

CHRISTIAN (sitting beside her on the bench. A silence):
  I love you.

ROXANE (closing her eyes):
  Yes, speak to me of love.

CHRISTIAN:
  I love thee.

ROXANE:
  That is the theme.
  Embroider, embroider.

CHRISTIAN:
  I love you...

ROXANE:
  Embroider!

CHRISTIAN:
  I love thee so much.

ROXANE:
  No doubt! And then?

CHRISTIAN:
  And then... I should be so happy
  If you loved me!—Tell me, Roxane, that thou lovest me!

ROXANE (pouting):
  You offer me gruel when I had hoped for creams!
  Tell me somewhat how you love me?...

CHRISTIAN:
  Why... very much.

ROXANE:
  Oh!... Unlabyrinth your feelings!

CHRISTIAN (having drawn closer and devouring the fair nape of her neck with his eyes):
  Thy neck!
  I should like to kiss it!...

ROXANE:
  Christian!

CHRISTIAN:
  I love thee!

ROXANE (about to rise):
  Again!

CHRISTIAN (quickly, holding her back):
  No! I do not love thee!

ROXANE (sitting down again):
  That is fortunate!

CHRISTIAN:
  I adore thee!

ROXANE (rising and moving away):
  Oh!

CHRISTIAN:
  Yes... I am becoming foolish!

ROXANE (dryly):
  And that displeases me!
  As it would displease me if you became ugly.

CHRISTIAN:
  But...

ROXANE:
  Go and gather up your fugitive eloquence!

CHRISTIAN:
  I...

ROXANE:
  You love me, I know. Farewell.
  (She goes toward the house.)

CHRISTIAN:
  Not yet!
  I shall tell you...

ROXANE (pushing the door open to go inside):
  That you adore me... yes, I know.
  No! No! Go away!

CHRISTIAN:
  But I...
  (She shuts the door in his face.)

CYRANO (who returned a moment ago without being seen):
  It is a success.



Scene 3.VI.

Christian, Cyrano, the pages, for a moment.


CHRISTIAN:
  Help!

CYRANO:
  No, sir.

CHRISTIAN:
  I shall die if I do not regain
  Her favor this very instant...

CYRANO:
  And how the devil can I
  Teach you this very instant?...

CHRISTIAN (seizing his arm):
  Oh! There, look, see!
  (The balcony window has lit up.)

CYRANO (moved):
  Her window!

CHRISTIAN (shouting):
  I am going to die!

CYRANO:
  Lower your voice!

CHRISTIAN (very softly):
  Die!...

CYRANO:
  The night is dark...

CHRISTIAN:
  Well?

CYRANO:
  It can be repaired.
  You do not deserve it... Get over there, wretch!
  There, in front of the balcony! I shall stand underneath...
  And prompt thee with thy words.

CHRISTIAN:
  But...

CYRANO:
  Be quiet!

THE PAGES (reappearing at the back, to Cyrano):
  Hey!

CYRANO:
  Hush!...
  (He signals to them to speak softly.)

FIRST PAGE (in a half whisper):
  We have just serenaded
  Montfleury!...

CYRANO (softly, quickly):
  Go and lie in ambush,
  One at that street corner and the other at this one;
  And if some troublesome passerby comes this way,
  Play a tune!

SECOND PAGE:
  What sort of tune, Mr. Gassendist?

CYRANO:
  A merry one for a woman, and a sad one for a man!
  (The pages disappear, one at each street corner.—To Christian):
  Call her!

CHRISTIAN:
  Roxane!

CYRANO (picking up pebbles and throwing them at the windowpanes):
  Wait! A few pebbles.



Scene VII.
